proposed_user_goal.graph_description:
A comprehensive knowledge graph for furniture manufacturing that integrates product management, supply chain tracking, and customer sentiment analysis. The graph models furniture products as compositions of various parts and components, with multi-supplier sourcing relationships and detailed customer sentiment data at both product and component levels.

Key entities include:
- Products: Furniture items with hierarchical part composition
- Parts/Components: Sub-assemblies and individual components that make up products
- Suppliers: Vendors providing parts with performance metrics (quality, delivery, pricing)
- Customers: End users providing feedback and reviews
- Reviews/Feedback: Customer sentiment data linked to products and specific parts
- Sentiment Scores: Quantified sentiment analysis results

Critical relationships capture:
- Product-to-part composition hierarchies
- Part-to-supplier sourcing with multiple supplier options per part
- Supplier performance tracking across quality, delivery, and cost dimensions
- Customer sentiment relationships to both products and individual components
- Traceability chains from customer complaints to specific suppliers and parts

Primary use cases:
1. Supplier impact analysis: Identify suppliers causing customer complaints through sentiment-to-supplier traceability
2. Quality correlation analysis: Analyze relationships between part quality issues and overall product satisfaction
3. Data-driven sourcing: Evaluate supplier performance across quality, delivery, and pricing for sourcing decisions
4. Product design optimization: Understand customer sentiment patterns for specific components and materials to guide design improvements

Data sources include customer reviews, supplier performance databases, product catalogs, inventory management systems, and structured/unstructured customer feedback from multiple channels.

_user_intent_conversation.content:
I want to build a comprehensive knowledge graph for furniture manufacturing that integrates product management, supply chain tracking, and customer sentiment analysis. The graph represents furniture products composed of various parts/components, with each part sourced from one or more suppliers. Customer feedback and sentiment data is captured at both product and part levels, enabling direct correlation between supplier performance and customer satisfaction.

Key entities include: Products (furniture items), Parts/Components (sub-assemblies and individual components), Suppliers (vendors providing parts), Customers, Reviews/Feedback, and Sentiment scores. Critical relationships track: product-part composition, part-supplier sourcing (including multiple suppliers per part), supplier performance metrics (quality, delivery times, pricing), customer sentiment about products and specific parts, and traceability from customer complaints to specific suppliers and parts.

The graph enables four primary use cases: (1) identifying suppliers that cause the most customer complaints through sentiment-to-supplier traceability, (2) analyzing correlations between part quality issues and overall product satisfaction scores, (3) making data-driven sourcing decisions by evaluating supplier performance across quality, delivery, and price dimensions, and (4) improving product design by understanding customer sentiment patterns for specific components and materials.

Data sources include customer reviews, supplier performance data, product catalogs, inventory systems, and structured/unstructured customer feedback from multiple channels.

_fact_extraction_conversation.content: Please propose fact types (relationship templates) for extraction from the review files based on the approved entity types.

## Fact Type Proposal

The review files cover 10 Scandinavian-styled furniture and home goods products. Reviews consistently mention specific parts such as drawer rails, slats, back panels, cushions, legs, handles, and shades, often with defect-level detail. The Helsingborg Dresser reviews are particularly notable, with multiple reviewers citing defective drawer rails and customer service explicitly acknowledging supplier quality issues — directly supporting CQ1 and CQ5. The proposed fact types create a full traceability chain from Reviewer → Review → Product, and from Review → Defect → Part → Supplier, enabling all seven competency questions to be answered. Key design choices include separating 'reports' (Review→Defect) from 'mentions_defect_in' (Review→Part) to allow both structured defect entities and lightweight part mentions, and using 'attributed_to' (Defect→Supplier) to capture supplier accountability signals found in review text.

**(Reviewer)-[authored]->(Review)**
  Captures the authorship relationship between a reviewer (identified by handle and location) and a specific review they wrote. Enables reviewer-level analysis such as identifying prolific reviewers or detecting patterns across reviews by the same person.

**(Review)-[evaluates]->(Product)**
  Links a review to the specific product being evaluated. This is the primary connection enabling product-level sentiment aggregation and satisfaction scoring (CQ2, CQ3, CQ4, CQ7).

**(Review)-[assigns_rating_to]->(Product)**
  Captures the numeric star rating a review gives to a product. Enables quantitative satisfaction scoring and correlation analysis (CQ2, CQ6).

**(Review)-[mentions_defect_in]->(Part)**
  Links a review to a specific part that is cited as problematic within the review text. Enables tracing negative sentiment to specific components (CQ4, CQ5, CQ7).

**(Review)-[reports]->(Defect)**
  Connects a review to a specific defect observed and described by the reviewer. Enables complaint counting and defect frequency analysis across reviews (CQ1, CQ2, CQ5).

**(Defect)-[observed_in]->(Part)**
  Associates a defect with the specific part where it manifests (e.g., drawer rails with rough edges, cracked slats). Enables part-level quality analysis and identification of problematic components (CQ2, CQ4, CQ7).

**(Part)-[belongs_to]->(Product)**
  Establishes the structural composition relationship between a part and the product it is a component of. Enables tracing part-level defects up to product-level satisfaction impact (CQ2, CQ4, CQ5, CQ7).

**(Supplier)-[supplies]->(Part)**
  Links a supplier to the part they manufacture or provide. Core relationship for supplier performance analysis and sourcing decisions (CQ1, CQ3, CQ5, CQ6).

**(Defect)-[attributed_to]->(Supplier)**
  Associates a defect with the supplier responsible for the defective part, based on review text or customer service disclosures (e.g., 'issues with a supplier'). Enables direct supplier accountability tracking (CQ1, CQ5).

**(Review)-[references_sentiment_about]->(Part)**
